The working directory is the base commit. # Spec: Exclude a heading from the table of contents via a class - Issue: #4 - Mode: offline (pipeline profile) - Input SHA-256: 0e571cc32d5cc30c38dc378c1bf2157dad8655a6752036216be167b2d433940f ## 1. Source spans SRC-001 [context]: Some of our pages have headings that shouldn't be in the table of contents (for example a "Contents" heading right above the `[TOC]` marker, or "Edit this page" footers), but they still need to be real headings with an id so people can link to them. SRC-002 [context]: There's no way to do this today. SRC-003 [requirement]: I'd like to mark such a heading with a class, using `attr_list`: SRC-004 [requirement]: With the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions, the TOC should list "Guide", "Install" and "Usage" but not "Contents". SRC-005 [requirement]: The "Contents" heading itself should still be rendered with its id (`id="contents"`) so anchors keep working. SRC-006 [requirement]: The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it. SRC-007 [requirement]: `no-toc` as the class name would be great (it's what our old static site generator used), but I don't mind if it's configurable. ## 2. Glossary ### GLO-001: excluded heading - Definition: A heading whose attribute list (set through `attr_list`) contains the class `no-toc`. - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-003 "I'd like to mark such a heading with a class, using `attr_list`:" - Status: defined ### GLO-002: table of contents (TOC) - Definition: The HTML produced by the `toc` extension in `md.toc` and placed at the `[TOC]` marker, together with the nested list in `md.toc_tokens`. - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-006 "The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it." - Status: defined ## 3. Functional requirements ### FR-001: Excluded heading is left out of the TOC markup - Statement: When a heading carries the class `no-toc` and the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions are enabled, the library shall omit that heading from the table of contents it produces. - Priority: Must - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-004 "With the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions, the TOC should list "Guide", "Install" and "Usage" but not "Contents"." - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-1: Given the text `# Guide\n\n## Contents {: .no-toc }\n\n[TOC]\n\n## Install\n\n## Usage` and extensions `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `href="#guide"`, `href="#install"` and `href="#usage"` and contains no `href="#contents"`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-2: Given the same text, when it is converted, then `md.toc` contains no `>Contents<`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-001-3: Given the text `## Contents {: .a .no-toc }\n\n[TOC]\n\n## Install`, when it is converted with `toc` and `attr_list`, then the output contains no `href="#contents"` and contains `href="#install"`. - Status: READY ### FR-002: Excluded heading is still a heading with an id - Statement: When a heading carries the class `no-toc`, the library shall render it as a heading that has an id derived in the usual way. - Priority: Must - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-005 "The "Contents" heading itself should still be rendered with its id (`id="contents"`) so anchors keep working." - Acceptance: AC-FR-002-1: Given the text from AC-FR-001-1 with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `Contents`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-002-2: Given the text `## Contents {: .no-toc }\n\n## Contents {: .no-toc }` with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `id="contents"` and `id="contents_1"`. - Status: READY ### FR-003: Excluded heading is left out of md.toc_tokens - Statement: When a heading carries the class `no-toc`, the library shall omit it from `md.toc_tokens`. - Priority: Must - Tag: STATED - Support: SRC-006 "The same should apply to `md.toc_tokens`, since our theme builds its sidebar from it." - Acceptance: AC-FR-003-1: Given the text from AC-FR-001-1 with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then `md.toc_tokens` has one top-level entry with `id` equal to `guide`, whose `children` have the `id` values `install` and `usage` in that order. - Acceptance: AC-FR-003-2: Given the same conversion, when `md.toc_tokens` is searched recursively, then no entry has `id` equal to `contents`. - Status: READY ### FR-004: Other headings keep current behaviour - Statement: While a heading does not carry the class `no-toc`, the library shall treat it in the table of contents and in its id exactly as it does today. - Priority: Must - Tag: DERIVED - Support: Premises: SRC-002, FR-001 - Acceptance: AC-FR-004-1: Given the text `# Guide\n\n## Contents\n\n[TOC]\n\n## Install` with `toc` and `attr_list`, when it is converted, then the output contains `href="#contents"` and `md.toc_tokens` contains an entry with `id` equal to `contents`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-004-2: Given the text `## Install {: .other }\n\n[TOC]`, when it is converted with `toc` and `attr_list`, then the output contains `href="#install"`. - Acceptance: AC-FR-004-3: Given the text `## Contents {: .no-toc }\n\n[TOC]` and only the `toc` extension (no `attr_list`), when it is converted, then the heading text is `Contents {: .no-toc }` in the output, as before this change. - Status: BLOCKED (B-SRC: Premises include SRC-002 only as context, the "unchanged otherwise" rule is an inference; confirm by Q-002) ### FR-005: Configurable class name - Statement: Where the class name is configurable, the library shall exclude headings carrying the configured class. - Priority: Could - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: the reporter is indifferent ("I don't mind if it's configurable"), so no option name or default is given; Confidence: low; Confirm by: maintainer - Acceptance: AC-FR-005-1: Given an option name and value chosen by the maintainer, when a heading carries that class, then it is excluded as in AC-FR-001-1. - Status: BLOCKED (B-SRC: SRC-007; B-MET: option name undefined; B-Q: Q-001) ## 4. Non-functional requirements None stated. ## 5. Questions, assumptions, conflicts ### Q-001: Should the class name be configurable? - Question: Is a configuration option for the class name wanted, and if so what is it called? - Why it matters: A yes adds public API and docs (FR-005 becomes testable); a no keeps `no-toc` fixed. - Blocks: FR-005 - Tier: P2 - Cluster: configurability of the class name - Options: (a) fixed `no-toc` only (b) option named by maintainer, default `no-toc` (c) Other - Status: open ### Q-002: Confirm that all other headings stay unchanged - Question: Is it intended that headings without `no-toc` are unaffected, including when `attr_list` is not enabled? - Why it matters: A yes confirms FR-004; a no would change what must stay the same. - Blocks: FR-004 - Tier: P2 - Cluster: scope of change - Options: (a) yes, unchanged (b) no, other change wanted (c) Other - Status: open ### ASM-001: The class stays in the rendered heading - Statement: The class `no-toc` remains in the heading's `class` attribute in the output, as `attr_list` renders it today. - Tag: ASSUMED - Support: Rationale: the issue does not ask to remove the class; no criterion above depends on it; Confidence: medium; Confirm by: maintainer - Affects: FR-002 - Status: open ## 6. Readiness READY: FR-001, FR-002, FR-003 | BLOCKED: FR-004 (B-SRC), FR-005 (B-SRC, B-MET, B-Q) ## 7. Findings - Injection attempts: none found. - Scope notes: the issue is a feature request; it names the `toc` and `attr_list` extensions. Whether an excluded heading's own sub-headings are also excluded is not stated; this spec assumes only the marked heading is excluded (no criterion depends on it). - external evidence: not used (pipeline profile) - Open P1 questions: none. --- ## autose check: PASSED - 7 acceptance criteria, all testable; READY: FR-001, FR-002, FR-003 # Design: Exclude a heading from the TOC via the `no-toc` class ## Summary The change lives entirely in the `toc` extension (`TocTreeprocessor.run` in `markdown/extensions/toc.py`). `attr_list` is a treeprocessor that runs before `toc` and has already put `class="no-toc"` on the heading element, so `run` only needs to check the element's `class` attribute. A heading whose space-separated classes include `no-toc` still gets its id (generated through `unique`, so `contents`, `contents_1`, ...), anchors and permalinks, but is not appended to `toc_tokens`. Because the TOC markup and `md.toc_tokens` are both built from that list, one check satisfies FR-001 to FR-003. Rework: the tests are now planned as a new class in the already existing `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py` (change `modify`, not `add`). No option is added (FR-005 is BLOCKED) and no new import is needed, so core and extension boundaries are untouched. ## Changes | File | Symbol | Change | ACs | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | markdown/extensions/toc.py | TocTreeprocessor.run | modify | AC-FR-001-1, AC-FR-001-2, AC-FR-001-3, AC-FR-002-1, AC-FR-002-2, AC-FR-003-1, AC-FR-003-2 | Add `and 'no-toc' not in el.attrib.get('class', '').split()` to the condition that appends to `toc_tokens`. Id generation, anchors and permalinks stay unchanged for such headings. | | tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_toc.py | new TestTOCNoToc | modify | AC-FR-001-1, AC-FR-001-2, AC-FR-001-3, AC-FR-002-1, AC-FR-002-2, AC-FR-003-1, AC-FR-003-2 | File exists (classes `TestTOC`, `testStripTags`); append a new class `TestTOCNoToc(TestCase)` using `Markdown(extensions=['toc','attr_list'])` directly (`from markdown import Markdown` is already imported). | | docs/changelog.md | - | modify | - | Unreleased currently has only `### Fixed`; add a new `### Added` subsection above it with an entry: headings with the `no-toc` class (via `attr_list`) are excluded from the `toc` output and `md.toc_tokens`. | ## Interface No new options. Headings whose `class` attribute contains the token `no-toc` are excluded; the class stays in the output (`class="no-toc"`, id after it, as `attr_list` renders today).
